title.en: The Subjunctive and Hypothetical Forms (suggest that he see, It’s time we left, as if he knew)
title.es: El subjuntivo y las formas hipotéticas (suggest that he see, It’s time we left, as if he knew)

text.en: The English subjunctive is small, but it is useful for Spanish speakers, because the Spanish “subjuntivo” often shows up here too. There are three main cases. The mandative subjunctive after insist, suggest, demand, recommend and it is essential: “I suggest that he see the doctor.” (the verb is the base form in every person). After it’s time, would rather and as if a past form is used with a present meaning: “It’s time we left.”, “I’d rather you stayed.”, “He talks as if he knew everything.”
text.es: El subjuntivo del inglés es pequeño, pero útil para hispanohablantes, porque el «subjuntivo» del español suele aparecer también aquí. Hay tres casos principales. El subjuntivo mandativo después de insist, suggest, demand, recommend y it is essential: «I suggest that he see the doctor.» (el verbo va en forma base en todas las personas). Después de it’s time, would rather y as if se usa una forma de pasado con sentido de presente: «It’s time we left.», «I’d rather you stayed.», «He talks as if he knew everything.»

title.en: The mandative subjunctive: suggest, insist, demand, recommend + that + base form
title.es: El subjuntivo mandativo: suggest, insist, demand, recommend + that + forma base

text.en: In the that-clause the verb is the base form in every person, also in the third person (no -s). Negative: not + base verb, without do. British English often uses should too: “I suggest that he should see…”.
text.es: En la cláusula con that el verbo va en forma base en todas las personas, también en la tercera (sin -s). Negación: not + verbo base, sin do. El inglés británico usa a menudo también should: «I suggest that he should see…».

examples.es: I suggest that he see the doctor.

tr.en: I suggest that he see the doctor.
tr.es: Sugiero que vaya al médico.

examples.es: She insisted that he not be late.

tr.en: She insisted that he not be late.
tr.es: Insistió en que no llegara tarde.

text.en: The same applies after “it is essential / vital / important / necessary that”: “It is essential that every student be present.”
text.es: Lo mismo vale después de «it is essential / vital / important / necessary that»: «It is essential that every student be present.»

examples.es: It is essential that every student be present.

tr.en: It is essential that every student be present.
tr.es: Es esencial que todos los estudiantes estén presentes.

tr.en: The manager demanded that the report be finished by Friday.
tr.es: El gerente exigió que el reporte estuviera listo para el viernes.

text.en: After it’s time and it’s high time the past form has a present meaning: the time is now. “It’s time we left.” Impersonal: “It’s time to leave.”
text.es: Después de it’s time e it’s high time la forma de pasado tiene sentido de presente: es hora ahora. «It’s time we left.» Impersonal: «It’s time to leave.»

tr.en: It's time we left.
tr.es: Ya es hora de que nos vayamos.

examples.es: It's high time you started looking for a job.

tr.en: It's high time you started looking for a job.
tr.es: Ya es más que hora de que empieces a buscar trabajo.

text.en: For another person’s action: would rather + subject + past simple. For your own action: would rather + base verb without to.
text.es: Para la acción de otra persona: would rather + sujeto + pasado simple. Para tu propia acción: would rather + verbo base sin to.

title.en: As if, as though and the fixed subjunctives
title.es: As if, as though y los subjuntivos fijos

text.en: In an unreal comparison a past form or were is used, and for the past the past perfect: “as if he knew”, “as if she had seen a ghost”. Fixed forms: “Long live the king!”, “Come what may”, “If need be”.
text.es: En una comparación irreal se usa una forma de pasado o were, y para el pasado el past perfect: «as if he knew», «as if she had seen a ghost». Formas fijas: «Long live the king!», «Come what may», «If need be».

examples.es: He talks as if he knew everything.

tr.en: He talks as if he knew everything.
tr.es: Habla como si lo supiera todo.

examples.es: Come what may, we will go.

tr.en: Come what may, we will go.
tr.es: Pase lo que pase, iremos.

text.en: “That he sees” is common in casual speech, but the polished, standard form is the base form: “that he see”. The negative is not “doesn’t see” but “not see”.
text.es: «That he sees» es común en el habla informal, pero la forma estándar y cuidada es la forma base: «that he see». La negación no es «doesn’t see» sino «not see».

text.en: Spanish influence: the Spanish “quiero que vengas” is not a subjunctive in English but “I want you to come”. After want, expect and tell comes object + to-infinitive, not a that-clause.
text.es: Influencia del español: el «quiero que vengas» del español no es subjuntivo en inglés sino «I want you to come». Después de want, expect y tell va objeto + to-infinitivo, no una cláusula con that.

speak.en: The English subjunctive is small but useful. After «insist», «suggest», «demand» and «recommend», and after «it is essential that», the verb is the base form in every person: «I suggest that he see the doctor». After «it's time», «would rather» and «as if» a past form is used with a present meaning: «It's time we left», «I'd rather you stayed», «He talks as if he knew everything». Fixed forms: «Long live the king» and «Come what may».
speak.es: El subjuntivo del inglés es pequeño pero útil. Después de «insist», «suggest», «demand» y «recommend», y después de «it is essential that», el verbo va en forma base en todas las personas: «I suggest that he see the doctor». Después de «it's time», «would rather» y «as if» se usa una forma de pasado con sentido de presente: «It's time we left», «I'd rather you stayed», «He talks as if he knew everything». Formas fijas: «Long live the king» y «Come what may».

items.sentence: I suggest that he ___ the doctor.

why.en: After suggest that the verb is the base form: that he see.
why.es: Después de suggest that el verbo va en forma base: that he see.

seeing.en: “That he seeing” is not correct; you need a finite or base form, not -ing.
seeing.es: «That he seeing» no es correcto; hace falta una forma conjugada o base, no -ing.

to see.en: “That he to see” is not correct; after that there is no to-infinitive.
to see.es: «That he to see» no es correcto; después de that no va to-infinitivo.

tr.en: I suggest that he see the doctor.
tr.es: Sugiero que él vea al médico.

items.sentence: She insisted that he ___ be late.

why.en: The negative of the subjunctive: not + base verb.
why.es: La negación del subjuntivo: not + verbo base.

didn't.en: “Didn’t be” is not correct; didn’t cannot stand before be.
didn't.es: «Didn’t be» no es correcto; didn’t no puede ir antes de be.

won't.en: Won’t be refers to the future and is not a subjunctive.
won't.es: Won’t be se refiere al futuro y no es subjuntivo.

examples: He insisted that she not go.
I ask that you not tell.

tr.en: She insisted that he not be late.
tr.es: Ella insistió en que él no llegara tarde.

items.sentence: It is essential that every student ___ present.

why.en: After it is essential that the base form be: that every student be.
why.es: Después de it is essential that la forma base be: that every student be.

being.en: “That every student being” is not correct; you need a finite or base form.
being.es: «That every student being» no es correcto; hace falta una forma conjugada o base.

to be.en: “That every student to be” is not correct; after that there is no to-infinitive.
to be.es: «That every student to be» no es correcto; después de that no va to-infinitivo.

examples: It is vital that she be here.
It is important that he be calm.

tr.en: It is essential that every student be present.
tr.es: Es esencial que cada estudiante esté presente.

items.sentence: The manager demanded that the report ___ finished by Friday.

why.en: After demand that the base form be + a participle: that the report be finished.
why.es: Después de demand that la forma base be + un participio: that the report be finished.

been.en: “That the report been finished” is not correct; before been you would need have.
been.es: «That the report been finished» no es correcto; antes de been haría falta have.

being.en: “That the report being finished” is not correct; you need the base form (be).
being.es: «That the report being finished» no es correcto; hace falta la forma base (be).

examples: They demanded that it be done.
She asked that the door be locked.

tr.en: The manager demanded that the report be finished by Friday.
tr.es: El gerente exigió que el informe estuviera terminado para el viernes.

why.en: After it’s time a past form with a present meaning: It’s time we went.
why.es: Después de it’s time una forma de pasado con sentido de presente: It’s time we went.

going.en: “It’s time we going” is not correct; you need a finite verb form.
going.es: «It’s time we going» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada.

to go.en: “It’s time we to go” is not correct; either it’s time to go or it’s time we went.
to go.es: «It’s time we to go» no es correcto; o it’s time to go o it’s time we went.

tr.en: It's time we went home.
tr.es: Es hora de que nos fuéramos a casa.

items.sentence: It's high time you ___ looking for a job.

why.en: After it’s high time a past form: you started.
why.es: Después de it’s high time una forma de pasado: you started.

starting.en: “It’s high time you starting” is not correct; you need a finite verb form.
starting.es: «It’s high time you starting» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada.

to start.en: “It’s high time you to start” is not correct; you need it’s high time you started.
to start.es: «It’s high time you to start» no es correcto; hace falta it’s high time you started.

tr.en: It's high time you started looking for a job.
tr.es: Ya es hora de que empezaras a buscar trabajo.

why.en: Another person’s action: would rather + subject + past simple.
why.es: La acción de otra persona: would rather + sujeto + pasado simple.

staying.en: “I’d rather you staying” is not correct; you need a finite verb form.
staying.es: «I’d rather you staying» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada.

to stay.en: “I’d rather you to stay” is not correct; after would rather there is no to.
to stay.es: «I’d rather you to stay» no es correcto; después de would rather no va to.

tr.en: I'd rather you stayed here tonight.
tr.es: Preferiría que te quedaras aquí esta noche.

why.en: Your own action: would rather + base verb.
why.es: Tu propia acción: would rather + verbo base.

stayed.en: “I’d rather stayed” is not correct; for your own action you need the base verb.
stayed.es: «I’d rather stayed» no es correcto; para tu propia acción hace falta el verbo base.

to stay.en: “I’d rather to stay” is not correct; after would rather there is no to.
to stay.es: «I’d rather to stay» no es correcto; después de would rather no va to.

tr.en: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
tr.es: Preferiría quedarme en casa esta noche.

items.sentence: He talks as if he ___ everything.

why.en: An unreal comparison: as if + past simple.
why.es: Una comparación irreal: as if + pasado simple.

knowing.en: “As if he knowing” is not correct; you need a finite verb form.
knowing.es: «As if he knowing» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada.

to know.en: “As if he to know” is not correct; you need a finite verb form.

examples: She acts as if she owned it.

items.sentence: She looked as though she ___ a ghost.

why.en: An unreal comparison about the past: as though + past perfect.
why.es: Una comparación irreal sobre el pasado: as though + past perfect.

sees.en: Sees is present; looked points to the past.
sees.es: Sees es presente; looked señala el pasado.

has seen.en: Has seen has a result for now; looked points to the past, so you need had seen.
has seen.es: Has seen tiene un resultado para ahora; looked señala el pasado, por eso hace falta had seen.

examples: He looked as if he had cried.
She felt as though she had won.

tr.en: She looked as though she had seen a ghost.
tr.es: Ella se veía como si hubiera visto un fantasma.

items.sentence: He behaves as if he ___ the boss.

why.en: An unreal comparison with be: as if he were.
why.es: Una comparación irreal con be: as if he were.

being.en: “As if he being” is not correct; you need a finite verb form (were).
being.es: «As if he being» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada (were).

to be.en: “As if he to be” is not correct; you need a finite verb form (were).
to be.es: «As if he to be» no es correcto; hace falta una forma verbal conjugada (were).

examples: She acts as if she were queen.
He talks as if he were rich.

tr.en: He behaves as if he were the boss.

why.en: A fixed subjunctive: Long live the king!
why.es: Un subjuntivo fijo: Long live the king!

lives.en: “Long lives” is not the fixed form; you need the base form live.
